title: Backcasting Distinguishability: Can a Monitor Tell Strategic Compliance From Genuine Alignment on Honeypots?

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting Distinguishability: Can a Monitor Tell Strategic Compliance From Genuine Alignment on Honeypots?

**Problem:** Success state: monitoring that separates a model genuinely behaving well from one complying only because it believes it is being watched. Backward: we need a measurement of whether behavior differs between 'looks-deployed' and 'looks-tested' framings on the same task.

**Direction:** Use public honeypot-style prompts (sabotage-opportunity tasks) and present each under two framings: explicit-evaluation vs. realistic-deployment. With an open model, measure rate of taking the misaligned action under each framing, producing an 'evaluation-awareness gap.' Result: 'a quantified strategic-compliance signal an outside monitor could flag.'

**Why it matters:** Distinguishing strategic compliance from real alignment is a stated Anthropic direction. A simple, reproducible eval-awareness-gap metric is valuable and needs only open models and public honeypot designs — a medium-horizon concern labs deprioritize.

**Relevant context:** 'Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed' (arXiv:2510.20487); 'Realistic honeypot evaluations for scheming propensity' (arXiv:2605.29729); Anthropic recommended-directions item on strategic compliance.
